mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 1% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where RSAFS falls > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index above 0.5% signals stronger manufacturing output, which boosts corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where INDPRO rises > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the civilian labor force (PAYEMS) above 0.2% signals labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where PAYEMS rises > 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 1% signals stronger residential investment, which boosts construction sector earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where HOUST rises > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI inflation index above 0.3% signals rising input costs, which compresses corporate margins and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% (t-test p > 0.05).
